Why would fleets wipe out the fish that paid their bills?
Northern cod catches topped 800,000 tonnes in 1968 and fell to about 5,000 by 1998 (DFO).
Canada closed the fishery in July 1992; about 30,000 people in Newfoundland and Labrador lost work.
Garrett Hardin called it the tragedy of the commons (Science, 1968). Elinor Ostrom won the 2009 economics Nobel showing communities can manage commons.
In 2026, Canada set a 59,000-tonne northern cod quota as the stock reached DFO's healthy zone; conservation groups say recovery is still fragile.
Sources: Fisheries and Oceans Canada, Science (1968), Heritage NL, Nobel Prize.
